rows.why: No bet: we expect about 65.7 receiving yards vs the 79.5 line — not enough to clear the price (needs 53% to pay at -114)
rows.why_long: Hard Rock under 79.5 at -114 needs 53% to pay; fair after the vig 50%. Averaging 66.5 over the last 8 games, lower than 79.5 in 70% of them (raw 68%, shrunk 53%). BAL allows +5% to WRs → projects 65.7 (raw 67%, shrunk 53%).
why_points: The bet: Rec yds under 79.5 at -114. To make money it has to win 53% of the time. The betting market, with the sportsbook's cut removed, gives it 50%.
Game log, most recent first: 77, 27, 98, 75, 12, 96, 60, 109. Weighted average 66.5; went lower than 79.5 in 5 of 8 games (70% recency-weighted).
How much he swings: game to game he typically moves about ±31.1, so the line is 0.4 of those swings above his average (standard deviations) — a modest gap.
Matchup: BAL has allowed +5% vs the league average to WRs (already shrunk toward average for sample size).
PFF unit matchup, for context (in the 2023-25 test it added nothing to the projection, so it is not in the numbers): +3% on his average.
PFF: BAL plays man on 27% of coverage snaps (his opponents so far 25%); he gains 1.72 yds/route vs man and 2.04 vs zone → -0% from scheme.
PFF: BAL allows 1.72 yds/route to WRs after adjusting for the offenses it faced (league 1.57) → +6% against his usual opponents.

PFF: He runs 29% of his routes from the slot (1.82 yds/route there, 2.08 outside); BAL allows 1.61 yds/route to slot WRs and 1.70 outside (league 1.47 / 1.63, opponent-adjusted) → +3% vs his usual opponents.
Projection: we expect 65.7 receiving yards on average; in a typical game 56.3 (a few big games pull the average up, so the typical game is what we compare with the line) — 23.2 below the line.

Keeping it honest: on their own, recent games (form) say 68% and the matchup 67%. The sportsbooks are usually close to right, and these methods have only partly beaten them (weights measured on NFL week 2), so we pull them most of the way toward the market: form 53%, matchup 53%.
Bottom line: we give it 53% to win and it needs 53%. The edge is the difference: -0.1 points; that works out to about -0¢ per $1 bet over the long run.

rows.why: Small role: one or two plays decide this, so it's risky — no bet: we expect about 13.1 receiving yards vs the 17.5 line — not enough to clear the price (needs 53% to pay at -114)
rows.why_long: Hard Rock under 17.5 at -114 needs 53% to pay; fair after the vig 50%. Averaging 10.4 over the last 8 games, lower than 17.5 in 72% of them (raw 63%, shrunk 52%). DEN allows -8% to WRs → projects 13.1 (raw 65%, shrunk 53%).
why_points: The bet: Rec yds under 17.5 at -114. To make money it has to win 53% of the time. The betting market, with the sportsbook's cut removed, gives it 50%.
Game log, most recent first: 30, 16, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 19. Weighted average 10.4; went lower than 17.5 in 6 of 8 games (72% recency-weighted).
Trending up: last 3 games average 15.3 vs 3.8 in the games before.
How much he swings: game to game he typically moves about ±12.3, so the line is 0.6 of those swings above his average (standard deviations) — a modest gap.
Market: DraftKings make this side 50% once their cut is removed; Hard Rock's price needs 53%. Hard Rock charges more than the market for this side.
Matchup: DEN has allowed -8% vs the league average to WRs (already shrunk toward average for sample size).
PFF unit matchup, for context (in the 2023-25 test it added nothing to the projection, so it is not in the numbers): -7% on his average.
PFF: DEN plays man on 27% of coverage snaps (his opponents so far 27%); he gains 1.25 yds/route vs man and 1.44 vs zone → -0% from scheme.
PFF: DEN allows 1.40 yds/route to WRs after adjusting for the offenses it faced (league 1.57) → -9% against his usual opponents.

PFF: He runs 23% of his routes from the slot (1.17 yds/route there, 1.27 outside); DEN allows 1.42 yds/route to slot WRs and 1.46 outside (league 1.47 / 1.63, opponent-adjusted) → -7% vs his usual opponents.
Projection: we expect 13.1 receiving yards on average; in a typical game 8.4 (a few big games pull the average up, so the typical game is what we compare with the line) — 9.1 below the line.

Keeping it honest: on their own, recent games (form) say 63% and the matchup 65%. The sportsbooks are usually close to right, and these methods have only partly beaten them (weights measured on NFL week 2), so we pull them most of the way toward the market: form 52%, matchup 53%.
Bottom line: we give it 53% to win and it needs 53%. The edge is the difference: -0.4 points; that works out to about -1¢ per $1 bet over the long run.
rows.glance_head: Pass: the line looks about right (we expect about 8.4 in a typical game vs the 17.5 line).
